context.guidance: Protect each Tier A and Tier B Personal Data Element at field or column level before it is stored, with keys held outside the data store, so that a database dump or a restored backup does not reveal the values. Disk or volume encryption protects only the storage medium, so it lowers severity without clearing the Finding. Until DPDP §44(2) omits IT Act §43A, that section's reasonable-security duty applies alongside Rule 6(1)(a).

value.fix: The evidence shows only `SecurityQuestionId` (an INTEGER foreign key to a question lookup table), so it is not itself the sensitive value. The Tier A/B exposure is most likely the security answer stored alongside it. Locate that sibling column in the same model and, before persistence, either (1) hash it with a salted, slow algorithm such as argon2id or bcrypt, since it only needs verification, or (2) if the plaintext must be recoverable, encrypt it at field level with AES-256-GCM using a key held in an external KMS/HSM, outside the database. Apply the same treatment to any other Tier A/B columns in this model. Leave `SecurityQuestionId` as a plain integer reference unless it can reveal sensitive information. Disk or volume encryption alone does not clear this finding, because a database dump or restored backup would still expose the values. Verify by inserting a test record, confirming the raw column in the database is ciphertext or a hash, and confirming that a dump or backup restore does not reveal the answer. Until DPDP §44(2) removes IT Act §43A, also document the reasonable-security measures under Rule 6(1)(a).
